themes_detail.label: Tree Crisis: Overgrown Branches & Deaths Spike
themes_detail.summary: Crown Heights is experiencing an acute tree maintenance emergency this week and last week, with overgrown tree/branch complaints up 2300% (15 complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average) and dead/dying tree complaints up 2300% (3 complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average), suggesting either storm damage, seasonal neglect, or systemic Parks Department underresourcing.
evidence: Overgrown Tree/Branches: 15 complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score 20.65, up 2300%)
Dead/Dying Tree: 3 complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score 8.69, up 2300%)
Illegal Tree Damage: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (z-score 3.89, up 380%)
Spike concentrated in most recent 1-2 weeks, not gradual trend
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about tree maintenance backlog and response times; compare to citywide tree complaint trends
Canvass Crown Heights streets to document which blocks are most affected; photograph hazardous branches and dead trees
Talk to residents about safety concerns—overgrown branches near schools, playgrounds, or over parked cars and sidewalks

themes_detail.label: Homelessness Complaints Spike 485%
themes_detail.summary: Over the past week, complaints about homeless person assistance jumped 485% (19 complaints last week vs. 3.2 weekly average, z-score 7.48), suggesting either a sudden visible increase in street homelessness or a shift in resident reporting, and aligning with long-standing community board requests for expanded homeless facilities.
evidence: Homeless Person Assistance complaints: 19 last week vs. 3.2 weekly average (z-score 7.48, up 485%)
Community Board has repeatedly requested 'Other facilities for homeless' from Department of Homeless Services—chronic unmet need
Spike is recent (last week) and statistically dramatic
reporting_angles: Map the 19 complaints geographically; identify if spike is concentrated near specific parks, transit hubs, or shelter locations
Interview DHS about bed capacity, outreach efforts, and why Crown Heights may be seeing an influx
Talk to affected residents and business owners about specific incidents; identify whether complaints reflect new encampments, behavioral issues, or other concerns

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signs Spike 700%
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints tripled this week alone (3 complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average, z-score 3.77, up 700%), indicating possible recent vandalism, storm damage, or maintenance gap that could affect pedestrian and driver safety.
evidence: Street Sign - Missing: 3 complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score 3.77, up 700%)
Spike concentrated in this week only; no prior weeks show similar pattern
Low absolute volume (3 complaints) but statistically significant deviation
reporting_angles: Field check: Walk key intersections in Crown Heights (near Atlantic Ave development area, major transit corridors) to document missing stop signs, street name signs, or directional signage
Query DOT on recent work orders; determine if this is vandalism-driven or maintenance-related
Check if spike correlates with weekend traffic incidents or safety complaints

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Complaints Up 380%
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged 380% last week (9 complaints vs. 1.9 weekly average), clustering with the broader tree crisis spike and suggesting possible construction activity, unpermitted pruning, or deliberate damage.
evidence: Illegal Tree Damage: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (z-score 3.89, up 380%)
Appears alongside Overgrown Tree/Branch and Dead/Dying Tree spikes, suggesting interconnected crisis
466 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (274 alterations) may include unpermitted tree work near development sites
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 9 illegal tree damage complaints with active DOB permits and development sites, especially Atlantic Ave FRESH project
Interview Parks Enforcement on enforcement actions taken; quantify response time to damage complaints
Document specific locations and patterns: are damages concentrated near construction zones or scattered?

themes_detail.label: Paint/Plaster Maintenance Dropped 62%
themes_detail.summary: Paint and plaster complaints fell 62% this week (15 complaints vs. 39.5 weekly average), a counterintuitive dip that may reflect reduced resident complaint-filing or a shift in maintenance priorities, and warrants tracking to distinguish between genuine improvement and reporting attrition.
evidence: PAINT/PLASTER: 15 complaints this week vs. 39.5 weekly average (z-score -3.64, down 62%)
Anomalous dip; unclear whether it reflects actual improvement or decline in complaint reporting
Simultaneous drops in DOOR/WINDOW (down 56%) and Traffic Signal Condition (down 65%) suggest possible reporting system issue or seasonal shift
reporting_angles: Monitor over next 2 weeks to confirm if dip is sustained (genuine improvement) or aberration
Spot-check Crown Heights buildings for exterior paint/plaster conditions to reality-test the complaint data
